USMEvaluation class

Source: R/usm_evaluation.R
USMEvaluation.Rd

Internal class. Detects USMs (situations) where the model performance on a given variable is very degraded compared to a reference version, relative to the overall performance of the species on that variable. Instantiated internally by evaluate.

Details

For each variable and each USM, the following ratio is computed:

$$RMSE\_ratio = 100 \times \frac{RMSE_{eval} - RMSE_{ref}}{RMSE_{species}}$$

where:

  • RMSE_eval: RMSE of the evaluated version, for the variable, on that USM.

  • RMSE_ref: RMSE of the reference version, for the variable, on that USM.

  • RMSE_species: RMSE of the evaluated version, for the variable, computed on the whole species (all USMs together).

A USM is considered as not passing the test if, for at least one variable:

  • RMSE_ratio > ratio_threshold (default 50%), OR

  • more than max_degraded_vars (default 3) variables have RMSE_ratio > degraded_threshold (default 20%) on that USM.

There is no minimum number of observations per USM. However, a variable that is not tested at the species level (fewer than 10 observations over the whole species, see RRmseComparison) is not tested on the USMs of that species either.

The class can be used in two ways:

  • Driven by eval_workspace/workspace, like SpeciesEvaluation: create with eval_workspace (or a pre-built workspace), then call run().

  • Manually, by directly providing stats_usm and stats_species (or a pre-computed data) for a single species, useful for unit testing.

Active bindings

degraded_vars

Data frame of variable/USM combinations (across all species) where rmse_ratio exceeds degraded_threshold (default 20%).

critical_vars

Data frame of variable/USM combinations (across all species) where rmse_ratio exceeds ratio_threshold (default 50%).

failed_usms

Data frame with columns species/situation for USMs that do not pass the test: either at least one variable with a ratio above ratio_threshold, or more than max_degraded_vars variables above degraded_threshold.

success

TRUE if the USM evaluation is successful, i.e. no USM failed the test for any species.

is_empty

TRUE if there is no data to evaluate.

skip_reason

Why no USM was evaluated (e.g. "no reference data"), or NULL if at least one species was evaluated.

USMEvaluation$new()

Create a new USMEvaluation object.

Usage

USMEvaluation$new(
  eval_workspace = NULL,
  species_filter = NULL,
  usms = NULL,
  var2exclude = NULL,
  percentage = 5,
  output_dir = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = NA,
  workspace = NULL,
  backend = NULL,
  logger = default_logger,
  species_evaluation = NULL,
  ratio_threshold = 50,
  degraded_threshold = 20,
  max_degraded_vars = 3,
  species = NULL,
  stats_usm = NULL,
  stats_species = NULL,
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

eval_workspace

Path to the evaluation workspace. Only used to build a default workspace when one isn't supplied. Providing this or workspace selects the evaluation mode; otherwise the object is built in manual mode from data/stats_usm+stats_species.

species_filter

Optional character vector of species to evaluate.

usms

Optional character vector of USMs to evaluate.

var2exclude

Optional character vector of variables to exclude.

percentage

Threshold (%) above which a variable is flagged as deteriorated vs. the reference.

output_dir

Output directory for the CSV export.

parallel, cores

Parallel execution options. Only used to build a default backend when one isn't supplied.

workspace

An optional EvalWorkspace object. If not provided, a new EvalWorkspace will be created from eval_workspace.

backend

An optional ParallelBackend object for parallel processing. If not provided, a new ParallelBackend will be created from parallel/cores.

logger

An optional logger object for logging messages. If not provided, the default logger will be used.

species_evaluation

Optional SpeciesEvaluation instance. If provided and already run(), its per-species statistics are reused instead of being recomputed from scratch (avoids re-reading the sim/obs/ref data and re-running CroPlotR's summary() for each species). Falls back to computing statistics independently for any species not found in species_evaluation (e.g. if it hasn't been run yet).

ratio_threshold

Numeric threshold (%) above which a single variable makes the USM fail. Default 50.

degraded_threshold

Numeric threshold (%) above which a variable is considered degraded. Default 20.

max_degraded_vars

Maximum number of degraded variables (ratio > degraded_threshold) tolerated per USM before it is considered failed. Default 3 (i.e. fails starting at 4 degraded variables).

species

Optional species name, used in manual mode (ignored in evaluation mode).

stats_usm

Manual mode: data frame of per-USM stats (RMSE, n_obs), for evaluated and reference groups, e.g. as returned by CroPlotR's summary method with all_situations = FALSE, stats = c("RMSE", "n_obs").

stats_species

Manual mode: data frame of species-level stats (RMSE, n_obs), e.g. as returned by CroPlotR's summary method with all_situations = TRUE (default).

data

Manual mode: optional pre-computed data frame (bypasses stats_usm/stats_species computation).

USMEvaluation$run()

Run the USM evaluation. This method computes, for each species found in the workspace (filtered according to species_filter/usms), the RMSE_ratio per variable and per USM, and stores the results internally.

Usage

USMEvaluation$run()

USMEvaluation$get_data()

Return the underlying data frame (one row per variable/USM/species combination, with columns: species, situation, variable, rmse_eval, rmse_ref, rmse_species, ratio, n_obs).

Usage

USMEvaluation$get_data()

USMEvaluation$export()

Export the USM evaluation data for deteriorated USMs, and a per-species USM pass/fail count summary, to CSV files.

The exported files are written to the csv subdirectory of the configured output directory: usm_thresholds.csv (the ratio_threshold/degraded_threshold/ max_degraded_vars this evaluation was configured with, so downstream reports can explain what "failed" means for this run), Deteriorated_USM.csv (only if at least one USM has deteriorated data), usm_summary.csv (species, total USMs, failed USMs, passed USMs), and failed_usms.csv (species, situation - the same USMs counted as "failed" in usm_summary.csv and reported by summary(), i.e. self$failed_usms; only written if at least one USM failed).
